body.data from earlier rounds: the procedure was written after round 2's verdict and checked against all earlier data; nothing here was computed before registration except the excluded pairs

hypotheses.accidents: every failure is at m <= 61, and failures are at most 1% of the registered predictions

body.rules: square: rules using L8, M8 or E4 (with N4, D4, A4, K8, B4, C4): every one whose call at m = 9 is not the full bound, and a sample of 100 of the rest (random.Random(3)); hexagon: all 112 using H4, H5 or H13 (with H1, H2, H3); triangle: all 112 using T7, T9 or T13 (with E, VO, VS)
body.seen before registration: the (rule, m) pairs computed in validate.py are excluded
body.sizes: odd m from 9 to 61, and from 63 to 141 where rule 90's or rule 150's period differs from the full bound; n = m (square), 2m (hexagon, triangle)
body.statement: atlas3.predict: the odd part of the period at odd part m is, in order: 1 if f = 0; the order of (a, b) mod m if f is a monomial; no prediction if f wraps mod m; for a dilation f = h(x^p, y^p), predict(h, m/p) if p | m, else predict(h, m); for an odd prime power f = g^k, q / gcd(q, k) with q = predict(g, m); for a complete split into one kind of 1D factor g, the symmetric 1D rule's period on m cells; no prediction for a split into mixed factors; otherwise the full bound 2^sord(m) - 1 (2^ord(m) - 1 if f is not symmetric). On the triangle f is s, where M^2 = s I.
body.title: Does the refined statement predict the periods of linear rules nobody has computed?
body.validation: validate.py, before registration: the new shells against direct simulation (60 of 60 pairs agree); OddExact against the odd part of atlas2.Exact's period (72 of 72); predict against every record of rounds 1 and 2 and round 1's discovery data at odd parts >= 9: 7,746 agree, 78 have no prediction, and the 4 that disagree are round 2's four accidents
